chapter: Pelican Hall and the Black Diamonds contest
title: The Pelican, its managers and the Black Diamonds band
summary: He tells how he joined Piron, describes the Pelican's owners and the Black Diamonds band of record-copying players he rehearsed.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: You see, well how them fellas in them days do them things is, just like what caused me to get into the Piran band was Walter Pichon came at the old place they called the Pelican, it was run by the Astoria. The Pelican was located on Grabin' Ramp, which you got a parking lot in there. That's another place used to run, much famous as the Bull, because some nights they'd have four bands that would play up there.

And the Pack House that was located on the court had the restaurant and ball and pool table downstairs. They called it, they was run by this fella by the name of Faubacher. And this fella, Bebe, William Ridgely's brother, he was the manager of the place. I think I don't know, remember his name? His first name? Yeah, his first name was Bebe Ridgely, his first name, he was a big tall, brown skin, heavy built man. But he was the manager of that place there, I can't think of his first name. But all I can tell you, yeah, he was originally a trombone player. Yeah, I've heard of Bebe, but I haven't heard of his brother. Yeah, yeah, well that was his brother run that place. Now them people run that place, and most of their dances run on Sundays and Monday nights, and plus a special occasion, but the houses run that. I see one night we played up there a band we made up called the Black Diamonds. And we took, we rehearsed for about a whole week, not every evening, to get all the record numbers like Lewis played. No music, this play by Hayes, hopped off the record. Now that band that consisted of during them times, Red Island on Trump and Henry Red Island on cornet, Yank on trombone, Paul Bones on E-Flat Alto sax, and Eddie Johnson on tenor, and Mercedes Gorman, the San Piano Piano, I'll tell you, replaced Jen Ness, he was living on Josephine near Drive on the piano, Eddie Morrell, which is my cousin, on the bass, Lawrence Morrell on the banjo, and I was on the drum.
What's the name of that band?
And we took every number with Lewis Song, put on the record, like Connett, Chop, Suey, and everything, I just can't think of all them things at present, and we got them records

They were all popular numbers. They were all popular numbers, and no mistake, and Red Island was a good corner player already, and we were working, and I got tired, I was coming to get disgusted, because I had a little call, and I had to bring my drum up there by Mercedes house in rehearsal every evening.
And the night we went on the Pelican to play it against the Pelican, the Silvertone Orchestra, with, that's when originally that split up from the original Tuxedo band. stuff
